insights.statement: Users restrict purchases to grocery on quick-commerce apps (e.g., JioMart) because non-grocery items they tried were non-returnable, defective, or had refunds/cancellations mishandled, and this was not disclosed clearly before purchase.
insights.mechanism: Users don't have a way to know upfront whether an item is returnable or how reliable the refund/cancellation process will be; the product page omits or buries this information. After being burned once (stuck with a wrong-size item, no refund after a week, a cancelled order with no return option), users don't treat it as a one-off failure — they generalize it into a rule ('never buy anything except grocery') and permanently narrow their behaviour to the one category where they've never been burned. The avoidance is a trust-based heuristic substituting for information they can't get at decision time.
insights.so_what: This is a trust/risk problem, not a discovery or catalog-breadth problem — users already know non-grocery categories exist, they've tried them and were penalized. Surfacing new categories more prominently, or improving search/browse, will not undo this; the fix has to attack the risk itself (clear, enforced returnability status pre-purchase, fast refund SLAs) or the behaviour will keep hardening category by category as more users get burned once each.
evidence_quotes: i was not okay with the size so returned the order but I didn’t get my refund amount till now it’s been 1week
never dare to buy anything except grocery from jio mart because either they don't send at all or its defective and the don't exchange or return
very bad service and most of the items are non returnable
insights.caveat: Sample is small (5 quotes) and conflates several distinct failure modes — refund delay, item defect, seller-side cancellation, and non-disclosure of return policy — that may have different root causes even though users experience them as one 'non-returnable = don't buy' lesson. Also appears anchored to a single platform (JioMart), so the generalization to quick-commerce broadly is unverified.
